hook.text: Cut your message into fixed-size blocks. Encrypt each block with the same key. That's a block cipher.

buildup.text: DES used 64-bit blocks and 56-bit keys. It dominated the 1970s until computers got fast enough to crack it.

discovery.text: AES replaced DES in 2001 with 128-bit blocks and keys up to 256 bits. Brute force is computationally impossible.

twist.text: Block ciphers need modes of operation. Encrypting blocks independently leaks patterns in repeated data.

climax.text: CBC, CTR, and GCM modes chain blocks together, hiding patterns and adding integrity checks.

punchline.text: Same key, fixed blocks, careful chaining.

quiz.question: Why do block ciphers need modes of operation?
options: To prevent identical blocks from producing identical ciphertext
